lesson_title: Ignoring files and keeping the project tidy

task.title: Tidying up the portfolio
task.description: You are in the ~/portfolio folder. The history already has 3 commits, and one of them has config.env with a database password committed by mistake. Some rubbish is lying next to it: node_modules/, dist/, debug.log, .DS_Store. Write the commands one per line: 1) Check the state of the repository. 2) Create a .gitignore that hides node_modules/, dist/, all *.log files, the secret files .env and config.env, and .DS_Store in any folder. 3) Stop tracking config.env so that the file stays on disk. 4) Create README.md: the first line is the heading # Portfolio, below it a line with a project description. 5) Rename about.htm to about.html with Git. 6) Add .gitignore and README.md to the index and make a commit. 7) Make sure the working directory is clean. Do not change the earlier commits.
task.starter_code:
# Write the commands one per line. Lines starting with # are comments.
# You are in the ~/portfolio folder. config.env with a password is already in the history,
# and node_modules/, dist/, debug.log, .DS_Store are lying next to it.

# 1. Check the state of the repository

# 2. Create .gitignore: node_modules/, dist/, *.log, .env, config.env, .DS_Store

# 3. Stop tracking config.env (the file must stay on disk)

# 4. Create README.md: a # heading and a description line

# 5. Rename about.htm to about.html with Git

# 6. Add .gitignore and README.md to the index and make a commit

# 7. Make sure the working directory is clean
task.setup:
sim.user.config["user.name"] = "Anna Karimova"; sim.user.config["user.email"] = "anna@example.com"; sim.user.config["init.defaultBranch"] = "main"; sim.run(`mkdir portfolio && cd portfolio && git init echo "

Anna Karimova

" > index.html mkdir css && echo "body { margin: 0; }" > css/style.css git add . && git commit -m "Add home page" echo "DB_USER=anna" > config.env echo "DB_PASSWORD=qwerty123" >> config.env git add . && git commit -m "Add database config" echo "

About me

" > about.htm git add about.htm && git commit -m "Add about page" mkdir -p node_modules/lodash && echo "module.exports = {};" > node_modules/lodash/index.js echo "Error: cannot connect to database" > debug.log mkdir dist && echo "body{margin:0}" > dist/style.min.css echo "mac" > .DS_Store `, { quiet: true });

tests.name: The .gitignore file is in the last commit
tests.fail: Add .gitignore to the index (git add .gitignore) and commit it - the rules must be stored in the repository.

tests.name: The node_modules/ dependencies and the dist/ build are ignored
tests.fail: Two lines in .gitignore: node_modules/ and dist/ - with a slash at the end and without typos.

tests.name: All .log files are ignored
tests.fail: The *.log pattern - the asterisk stands for any name.

tests.name: Secrets are ignored: config.env and .env
tests.fail: Add two lines to .gitignore: .env and config.env.

tests.name: .DS_Store is ignored in any folder
tests.fail: The line .DS_Store without a slash at the start - then the pattern works in all folders.

tests.name: The needed files are not ignored
tests.fail: The pattern is too broad: check that .gitignore has no lines like * or *.html.

tests.name: config.env is no longer tracked, but stays on disk
tests.fail: You need git rm --cached config.env: without --cached Git deletes the file itself from disk too.

tests.name: The rubbish did not get into the commit
tests.fail: First .gitignore, then git add. If the rubbish is already in the index - git rm -r --cached folder.

tests.name: README.md is committed: a heading and a description
tests.fail: README.md: the first line is a heading like # Portfolio, below it at least one line of description. Use cat > README.md << 'EOF'.

tests.name: about.htm is renamed to about.html
tests.fail: git mv about.htm about.html, then a commit.

tests.name: The history is not rewritten: the old commits are in place
tests.check: ["Add home page", "Add database config", "Add about page"].every((s) => repo.log().some((c) => c.subject === s)) && repo.log().length >= 4
tests.fail: Do not delete or change earlier commits: make changes with a new commit on top.

tests.name: The working directory is clean
tests.fail: After the commit git status must answer: nothing to commit, working tree clean. Everything needed is in the commit, the rubbish is in .gitignore.

tests.name: A different project: .env, logs/error.log and other rubbish are hidden, the working directory is clean
tests.check: repo.isIgnored(".env") && repo.isIgnored("logs/error.log") && repo.status().clean && repo.commit("HEAD").files["config.env"] === undefined && sim.read("~/portfolio/config.env") === "DB_USER=anna\nDB_PASSWORD=Secret-2026\n" && Object.keys(repo.commit("HEAD").files).every((p) => !p.startsWith("logs/") && p !== ".env" && !p.endsWith(".DS_Store"))
tests.fail: The rules must work for any project: *.log catches logs in any folder, .env is a secrets file.

sim.user.config["user.name"] = "Anna Karimova"; sim.user.config["user.email"] = "anna@example.com"; sim.user.config["init.defaultBranch"] = "main"; sim.run(`mkdir portfolio && cd portfolio && git init echo "

Anna Karimova

" > index.html mkdir css && echo "body { margin: 0; }" > css/style.css git add . && git commit -m "Add home page" echo "DB_USER=anna" > config.env echo "DB_PASSWORD=Secret-2026" >> config.env git add . && git commit -m "Add database config" echo "

About me

" > about.htm git add about.htm && git commit -m "Add about page" echo "API_KEY=sk-test-123" > .env mkdir logs && echo "500 Internal Server Error" > logs/error.log mkdir -p node_modules/react && echo "react" > node_modules/react/index.js mkdir dist && echo "console.log(1)" > dist/bundle.js echo "mac" > css/.DS_Store `, { quiet: true });

tests.name: The script ran without internal errors
tests.fail: Check the quotes and the EOF line at the end of cat > ... << 'EOF'.

hints: A multi-line file: cat > .gitignore << 'EOF', then the pattern lines, the last line is EOF.
Folders take a slash at the end: node_modules/ and dist/. All logs: *.log.
.gitignore does not hide a file that is already in the repository: git rm --cached config.env.
Renaming: git mv about.htm about.html - Git adds it to the index right away.
Before the commit, look at git status: the list should have new file: .gitignore, new file: README.md, deleted: config.env and renamed: about.htm -> about.html.

questions.question: Why do we need the .gitignore file?
options: It deletes unneeded files from disk
It lists files that Git should not notice among untracked files
It hides files from other users of the computer
It encrypts passwords in the repository
questions.explanation: .gitignore does not delete or encrypt anything: Git just stops showing such files in Untracked files and does not add them with git add .

questions.question: Match the .gitignore pattern with what it ignores.
pairs: All files with the .log extension in any folder
The build folder and everything inside it
Only todo.txt in the project root
An exception: do not ignore keep.log after all
questions.explanation: * means any characters, / at the end means only a folder, / at the start means from the root, ! is an exception to the rules above.

questions.question: What should NOT be stored in Git?
options: The .env file with API keys
The node_modules/ folder
README.md
The dist/ folder with the build
The .gitignore file
questions.explanation: Secrets, dependencies and build results are not stored in Git. README.md and .gitignore are part of the project, they are committed.

questions.question: config.env is already committed. You added the line config.env to .gitignore and changed the file. What will git status show?
options: Nothing: the file is ignored now
modified:   config.env - Git keeps watching the file
deleted:    config.env
An error: a file in .gitignore cannot be changed
questions.explanation: .gitignore affects only untracked files. A file that is already in the repository must be untracked: git rm --cached config.env.

questions.question: Enter the full command: stop tracking the config.env file in Git, but keep it on disk.
questions.explanation: --cached means remove only from the index. After the commit the file is no longer tracked, but it stays on disk.

questions.question: A password got into a commit that is already pushed to GitHub. You ran git rm --cached and made a new commit. What else is a must?
options: Nothing: the password is removed from Git
Change the password - the old commit with it stays in the history
Delete the .gitignore file
Run git add -f config.env
questions.explanation: A new commit does not change old ones: git show on the old commit will show the password. A leaked secret is considered compromised - it is changed.

questions.question:
What did Git print?

$ git add debug.log
The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files:
debug.log
hint: Use -f if you really want to add them.
options: The file is added to the index
The file is not added: it matches a .gitignore rule
The file is deleted
debug.log does not exist
questions.explanation: Git refused to add an ignored file and suggested the -f option in case you really need it.

questions.question: What is true about git mv about.htm about.html?
options: It renames the file on disk
It adds the rename to the index right away
git status will show renamed:    about.htm -> about.html
It creates a commit automatically
questions.explanation: git mv = mv + git add for both names. You still have to make the commit yourself.

questions.question: Match the command with the result.
pairs: Delete the file from disk and from the index
Remove from the index, keep on disk
Rename and prepare for the commit right away
questions.explanation: rm deletes, --cached keeps the file on disk, -r is needed for folders, mv renames.

questions.question: You created an empty images folder and ran git status. What will Git answer?
options: Untracked files: images/
nothing to commit, working tree clean
fatal: empty directory
new file: images
questions.explanation: Git stores only files, it does not see empty folders. To keep a folder, people put an empty .gitkeep file into it.

questions.question: What is the usual name of the empty file that is put into a folder so that Git keeps it in the repository? Enter the file name.
questions.explanation: .gitkeep is an agreement among developers, not a Git command: any file would do, but everyone understands this name.

questions.question: .gitignore has the lines logs/ and !logs/important.log. Will logs/important.log be tracked?
options: Yes, ! always cancels ignoring
No: if a folder is ignored as a whole, files inside it cannot be brought back with !
Yes, but only after git add -f
Git will report an error in .gitignore
questions.explanation: Git does not look into an ignored folder. You need to ignore the contents (logs/*) and then add the exception !logs/important.log.
